question: My marks are 78% in Class 12 and my family can spend Rs 1.5 lakh per year. Which engineering colleges am I eligible for?
note: Cutoff is a hard floor: C001 (82%) and C012 (88%) must be excluded at 78%. C003 and C009 pass both fee and cutoff.

question: What MBA options are there and what are the fees?
note: Similar-name trap: Ganga Institute of Commerce (C014) has no MBA and must not be confused with Ganga Valley University (C002).

question: List the government colleges that have hostel facilities.
note: C005 and C011 are government but have no hostel.

question: Does Ganga Valley University offer a PhD in Physics?
note: Not in the data; the system must say so rather than guess. (Doctoral scholars exist only at C009, engineering only.)

question: I can pay 60 thousand rupees per semester. Which colleges fit my budget?
note: Unit trap: 60k/semester = 1.2 lakh/year (2 semesters/year, assumption must be stated). C001 (1.45L) and C003 (1.32L) exceed it.

question: Which colleges offer scholarships or fee concessions for students from low-income families?
note: Answerable only from the free-text 'about' field. C004 (need-based alumni scholarship) is acceptable extra.

question: Which college has the lowest average placement package?
note: C006 reports 0 = not reported (medical college), NOT worst. Lowest reported figure is C007 at 2.8 LPA.

question: किन सरकारी कॉलेजों में हॉस्टल की सुविधा उपलब्ध है?
note: Multilingual check: Hindi question must retrieve correctly and be answered in Hindi.

question: What is the student-to-faculty ratio at Terai Technical University?
note: The dataset has no such field for C009; the system must refuse gracefully instead of inventing a number.

question: Can I study engineering somewhere for under Rs 50,000 a year? I scored 65%.
note: Only C005 fits fee+cutoff, but it awards diplomas, not degrees — the answer must disclose that explicitly. (C012 fits the fee but its 88% cutoff excludes a 65% student.)

question: Give me all the details about Kumaon Arts and Science College, Almora — hostel available, allocated prioritizing students from remote hill blocks.
note: Regression for a real bug: 'hiLL Blocks' used to substring-match the 'LLB' course token, tripping the course check into a false refusal. Full-profile lookups must return the whole record.

question: My family can spend 4 lakh in total for the whole course. Which B.Tech colleges fit?
note: Third unit style from the data dictionary: a TOTAL-course budget must not be silently treated as an annual ceiling — the answer must reason per-year (a 4-year B.Tech at 4L total means ~1L/year) and state the framing.

question: Which college has the highest placement AND also has a hostel?
note: ADVERSARIAL: two conditions plus a superlative. C012 (8.4 LPA, hostel Yes) is the answer; requires combining a max with a boolean filter, which top-k + a single superlative fact doesn't directly hand the model.

question: I'm a girl from a hill district and money is tight. What are my best options?
note: ADVERSARIAL: three soft constraints, all in free text — female concession (C003), hill-district scholarship (C013), low-fee government (C007). No structured field captures 'girl' or 'hill district'; success depends entirely on about-field retrieval. Known weak spot.

question: List the government colleges that do NOT have a hostel.
note: ADVERSARIAL: negation combined with a type filter. Only C005 and C011 are government AND hostel=No. Tests that negation handling and the government filter compose correctly.

question: Between the cheapest engineering college and the one with the best placement, which is the smarter choice?
note: ADVERSARIAL: subjective value judgement with no single right answer. A good response lays out the trade-off (C005 cheapest but diploma-only; C012 best placement, higher cutoff) rather than declaring a winner. Graded loosely; here to observe behaviour, not to guarantee a pass.

question: Which college has the best NIRF ranking?
note: ADVERSARIAL refusal: NIRF rank is not a field we hold. Must refuse gracefully, not substitute NAAC grade or placement as if it were a ranking.
